name: M.Rudra

sections.heading: Life and writing.
paragraphs: M. Rudra’s ‘Unshackled Dreams’ brings a voice of protest to Kabita Live. The poem begins with confinement and turns towards the unequal freedom offered to women and men. Its chains and darkening sky make social restriction feel immediate, while the speaker insists on the right to imagine a life beyond it.

An appeal to the Mahabharata stands beside the contemporary image of candles raised in protest. The contrast asks what public gestures can achieve when fear and judgment remain. The closing wish to dream freely gives the poem its direction: towards dignity and possibility, even while the conditions of freedom are still being questioned.
